blocks.x: Event-log forensics that turn system footprints into a defensible automation pipeline: conformance-checked, variant-ranked, ROI-screened — with kill reasons logged so the backlog your board funds is the backlog reality earned.
Your systems already recorded the truth about your processes

Process mining is evidence gathering, not workshop theater. The systems already record the truth: timestamps in the ERP, states in the ITSM tool, messages on the bus. We reconstruct the actual process from those logs, measure where time and rework concentrate, and price the automation candidates against the mined baseline rather than a manager's estimate.

The deliverable that matters is a ranked pipeline with kill reasons. Most mined candidates die on data quality, permission reality or volume math — recording why is as valuable as the shortlist, because it stops the same idea being re-proposed every year.
What follows is the mining discipline end to end: failure modes, the reference architecture of a mining pipeline, and the console that keeps the backlog honest between cycles.
Four ways mining programs produce fiction instead of pipelines
Mining fails as politics before it fails as statistics — each countermeasure below makes the output arguable in a steering meeting, which is where it has to survive.

blocks.x: Mining stack defaults — and when we deviate
Defaults favor replayable analysis over one-off consulting artifacts; deviation conditions are written because each one changes whether the mining can be re-run next quarter.

blocks.caption: Process & Task Mining: default stack and the conditions under which we deviate
rows: Event extraction
CDC + scheduled extracts into an event lake with XES mapping
Vendor mining tools' native connectors only for the pilot phase
Correlation
Deterministic case keys with documented join logic
Probabilistic matching only with a measured join-quality floor
Discovery
Inductive Miner variants + PM4Py for custom analyses
Hand-drawn BPMN as the source of truth — the log overrules it every time
Conformance
Token-replay + alignment-based conformance on the happy-path model
Frequency-only analysis — it hides the expensive rework loops
Monitoring
Streaming miner on bus telemetry with drift scoring
Quarterly batch mining for processes that genuinely change slowly
